items.title: ‘Let MACC, AGC look into it’: Anwar leaves Saravanan’s letter to authorities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today he would leave it to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) to examine a letter from MIC deputy president Datuk Seri M. Saravanan concerning allegations linking him to the recruitment of foreign workers. Anwar said he would refer the contents of the letter to the relevant authorities to ensure any investigation and prosecution proceeded according to their respective jurisdictions, Sinar Harian reported today. The former human resources minister said he had never been personally involved in the recruitment of foreign workers, nor had he involved any family members throughout his tenure.

items.title: Kulai crash death reclassified as murder; 13 suspects arrested including minors
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 28 — Police have arrested 13 people, including a 15-year-old girl, to assist in investigations into the death of a 17-year-old girl in Kulai last Tuesday, which has now been reclassified as a murder case. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the Kulai district police headquarters operations room received information from the public about a road accident involving a black Perodua Myvi at the Lingkaran Bulatan Persiaran Indahpura 4 at about 12.38 am. He said initial investigations found that the vehicle was driven by a 20-year-old man with four passengers, including the 17-year-old victim.

items.title: Friends face murder charge over killing of Indonesian man in Klang’s Telok Gong
items.summary: KLANG, Aug 28 — Two friends were charged at the Magistrate’s Court here today with the murder of an Indonesian man earlier this month. Muhd Asnawi Ghazali, 37, and Musa Ramli, 25, nodded in understanding after the charges were read out before Magistrate Siti Zubaidah Mahat. However, no plea was recorded from either accused, as the case falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.

items.title: Thousands watch National Day rehearsal at Dataran Putrajaya ahead of Aug 31 parade
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 28 — The excitement surrounding the 2026 National Day celebrations is building as crowds flock to the iconic Dataran Putrajaya to witness first-hand the preparations and parade rehearsals ahead of the historic celebration on Aug 31. Every time we take part in the National Day celebrations, it reminds us of the harmony, peace and unity among Malaysia’s various races that we enjoy today,” he said after completing the rehearsal. Members of the Malaysian Armed Forces (ATM) contingent march during the rehearsal for the National Day 2026 celebration at Dataran Putrajaya in Putrajaya on August 28, 2026.

items.title: Haze continues choking Malaysia as 19 areas see ‘Unhealthy’ air quality
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Nineteen air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded “unhealthy” air pollutant index (API) readings as of 1.30pm today, according to Department of Environment (DoE) data. The highest API reading nationwide was logged at Serian in Sarawak, which reached 181. Unhealthy levels across other states Beyond Sarawak and the Klang Valley, deteriorating air quality was observed across several northern and central states.

items.title: Heavy rain and strong winds expected across Johor, Sabah and Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning covering multiple states, effective until 4:00 pm today. In Johor, the warning covers Pontian, Kulai, Johor Bahru and Kota Tinggi. In Sarawak, affected areas include Bintulu and Sebauh in the Bintulu district; Miri, Subis, Beluru and Marudi in the Miri district; and Mukah, Dalat and Matu in the Mukah district.

items.title: Anwar begins two-day Penang visit with students, community events and Scout jamboree
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today began a two-day working visit to Penang packed with various engagements, including meetings with students, the Muslim community and local residents. The visit began with Friday prayers at Masjid Sembilang, Butterworth, at 1.30pm, followed by a “Temu Anwar Bersama Pelajar” session in conjunction with the Ambang Merdeka Sahabat Madani Programme at the Tuanku Bainun Teacher Education Institute campus in Bukit Mertajam at 4pm. Tomorrow, Anwar is scheduled to officiate the Permatang Pauh Skim Usahawan Bangkit programme at Dewan Yayasan Aman Penanti, Kubang Semang, at 10am.

items.title: Wisma Putra launches round-the-clock effort to trace 57 Malaysians after Nepal disaster
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Fifty-seven Malaysians are currently uncontactable following devastating floods in Nepal’s Rasuwa district, with Wisma Putra’s Operations Room now operating around the clock as diplomatic missions cross-check reports with Nepalese authorities. The ministry said local authorities had reported the rescue of 31 foreign nationals thus far. Wisma Putra said it had also received information that Malaysian nationals may have entered the affected areas through neighbouring China and India.

items.title: Nepal lists 51 Malaysians among 537 foreigners still out of contact after Himalayan floods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Nepal’s tourism authorities have released a list of 537 foreigners from more than 30 countries reported missing following the devastating floods in Rasuwa district. The list was published on the website of the Department of Tourism under Nepal’s Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation on Thursday evening under the headline “Tourist List (Out of Contact) in Bhotekoshi Flood”. They are: A Ganesan Anandan (M) Appannah A Muthaloo (M) Arunasalam Karuppiah (M) Azman Bin Karim (M) Balasingam Kesavan (M) Brabaakaran Krishnan (M) Eswary Mani Raj (F) Gunanesan Vellaisamy (M) Gunavathy Muthusamy (F) Inthumathy Subramaniam (F) Jason Ngeow (M) Kalai Mathe Karuppaiah (F) Kalaiselvi P Narayanasamy (F) Kannan Kerisna (M) Karunanithi Sundram (M) Kirubanithi Alagappan (M) Komathi Rethinam (F) Krishnan Vadivelu (M) Letchumy Sinnappan (F) Lingam Samykanoo (M) Malani M Vellu (F) Mangala Vanan Krishnasamy (M) Mohd Fakhrul Munir Bin Mohd Isa (M) Mohd Nohan Bin Salim (M) Mohd Padzil Bin Daros (M) Mohd Sani Bin Harul (M) Muhamad Nasir Bin Abdul Talib (M) Muhammad Haziq Bin Ismail (M) Murukan Supramaniam (M) Nahentran Ganasan (M) Navein Palani (M) Neelavany Marimuthu (F) Padmahwathi A Govindasamy (F) Poobalan Murgaya (M) Poornima Alagappan (F) Rajita Sivan (F) Raman Supramaniam (M) Ravindar Ayyavoo (M) S Gomathi Sitoralingam (F) S Ramu Sawasamy (M) Santhanaletchmi Tiruganasambandam (F) Saraswathi Nagaratnam (F) Saratha Alagappan (F) Shabuddin Bin Mun (M) Suguna Balan (F) Thanapalan Muthoo (M) Vallie Palaniasamy (F) Vanajah Vadival (F) Vennila Muniandy (F) Vijayan Perumal (M) Yougesvari Subramaniam (F) The list showed that India recorded the highest number of missing nationals at 178, followed by the United States (US) with 65 and Ukraine with 53.

items.title: Saravanan calls graft charges ‘wild accusations’, says facts will emerge in court
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Former human resources minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan today described the corruption charges against him as “wild accusations”, saying he was surprised by the three charges and had no personal relationship with the people named in them. Speaking to reporters after claiming trial to all three charges at the Sessions Court here, the Tapah MP said he would let the facts be brought before the court. Saravanan also appeared to suggest that the charges could be politically motivated.

items.title: ‘My only hope is they are safe’: A Malaysian family’s agonising wait for news after Nepal-Tibet floods
items.summary: BIDUR (Nepal), Aug 28 — They came to the Himalayas seeking spiritual renewal, drawn by Tibet’s sacred, snow-capped Mount Kailash. “I saw two buses carrying Indian pilgrims to Kailash Mansarovar,” said 27-year-old Laloma, a Nepali mother. The buses were swept away, she said.

items.title: Malaysia aims to push medical device exports beyond RM50b by 2030, says Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Malaysia should aim to surpass RM50 billion in medical device exports by 2030, up from RM34.54 billion recorded last year. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the export target was one of three ambitions proposed to measure the country’s progress in developing its medical technology (MedTech) industry by 2030. “But the next phase of export growth must increasingly come from higher-value products,” he said at the closing ceremony of the International Medical Device Exhibition and Conference (IMDEC) 2026 here today.

items.title: Husband and wife among seven held as Penang police seize drugs worth RM3.2m
items.summary: Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim said the couple were among four people arrested in an operation in Tanjung Tokong between August 15 and 16, Sinar Harian reported. “During the operation, police seized 38.3kg of cannabis powder, 11.47kg of cannabis flower, 4,004 Erimin 5 pills, 14kg of methamphetamine, 5kg of ketamine and 16kg of ecstasy pills. Dennis said all four suspects were remanded for 13 days from August 16 to 28 to assist investigations.

items.title: National Day parade preparations in Putrajaya nearly complete ahead of tomorrow’s full rehearsal, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 28 — Preparations for the 2026 National Day parade at Dataran Putrajaya are expected to be nearly 100 per cent complete by tomorrow’s dress rehearsal, with only a few minor aspects requiring fine-tuning, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said the improvements involved coordinating the movement distances between contingents to ensure the overall parade was conducted in a neater and more orderly manner. Insya-Allah, by tomorrow (the full rehearsal), we believe (preparations) will be nearly 100 per cent complete,” he said.

items.title: WCE expects more traffic as Malaysians hit the road for National Day, school holidays
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 28 — The West Coast Expressway (WCE) expects traffic on its operational stretches to exceed 150,000 vehicles a day during the 69th National Day celebrations and school holidays. Its Highway Operations head Syed Muhd Naguib Syed Mohd advised motorists to plan their journeys early and avoid peak hours, particularly from late afternoon to night. He said WCE would step up operational readiness along its open stretches, including 24-hour highway patrols, Emergency Response Teams (ERT) and continuous traffic monitoring.

items.title: Malaysian Fire Dept ready to deploy specialist rescue team to Nepal as nine hikers remain uncontactable
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 28 — The Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) is ready to deploy its Special Tactical Operation and Rescue Malaysia (STORM) team to Nepal at any time, even at short notice, should it receive instructions from the government. JBPM director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the deployment of the team, however, would be subject to a request from the Nepalese government as well as instructions and coordination by the Foreign Ministry and the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma). In a related development, Nor Hisham said JBPM had still been unable to contact the nine hikers, including two department officers, as well as a local agent in Nepal as of this morning.

items.title: Driver trapped, suffers broken arm in four-vehicle crash on Subang route towards Federal Highway
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — A driver was trapped and suffered a broken arm in a four-vehicle crash along the Subang route towards the Federal Highway this morning. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Ashrul Riezal Ashbar said the department received an emergency call at 9.24am before five personnel from the Subang Jaya Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene, according to Berita Harian today. “The fire engine arrived at 9.45am and found that the crash involved a tour bus and three cars.

items.title: New Batam-Penang flights to boost tourism, medical travel, says state exco
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 28 — Batik Air will launch direct flights between Batam and Penang from October 18, opening a new gateway for Penang to tap into the tourism market in Indonesia’s Riau Islands. State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the route, the first scheduled direct air link between Batam and Penang, would operate three times a week. He said the Batam-Penang route also had strong potential to support the state’s medical tourism sector, given Penang’s comprehensive medical facilities, professional healthcare services and well-established medical tourism ecosystem.

items.title: Kedah teacher transferred pending probe into Year Four pupil’s death after sports activity
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Aug 28 — A teacher believed to be involved in the case of an 11-year-old girl who allegedly died from a heart condition after being forced to participate in sports activities has been transferred pending the outcome of an investigation, according to the Kedah Education Department (JPN). A Kedah JPN spokesman said the teacher was transferred to another school shortly after an initial investigation, describing the move as an early intervention. Meanwhile, an internal school source said the incident involving the pupil happened on April 14, when she was reportedly involved in a selection trial for the 80-metre race for the school’s sports event.

items.title: Saravanan claims trial to three corruption charges involving RM1.097m, granted RM450,000 bail
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Former human resources minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan today claimed trial to three charges of corruptly receiving RM1.097 million in bribes linked to the approval of 1,000 foreign-worker quotas for a company. The three charges involve alleged bribes of RM150,000, RM350,000 and RM597,000, which the prosecution claims Saravanan received from Vectica Resources Sdn Bhd director Tan Teck Lim through Syed Amirul Syed Ahmad. According to the first charge, Saravanan allegedly received RM150,000 in cash from Tan through Syed Amirul on June 16, 2022, at Bukit Jalil Golf & Country Resorts.

items.title: Sarawak moves to tackle connectivity gaps in Limbang, Lawas
items.summary: LAWAS, Aug 28 — Sarawak’s telecommunications modernisation agenda is prioritising efforts to address connectivity disruptions in northern Sarawak, particularly in Limbang and Lawas. Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Awang Tengah Ali Hasan said the collaboration between the Ministry of Utilities and Telecommunications, Sarawak Digital Economy Corporation (SEDC) and Sarawak Energy Berhad (SEB) would help improve digital connectivity and government services. “We welcome the collaboration between SEB and SEDC to improve digital connectivity, particularly in northern Sarawak involving Limbang and Lawas.

items.title: Higher Education Ministry begins steps towards repeal of UUCA, halts student disciplinary proceedings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — The Higher Education Ministry (MOHE) is taking immediate steps to expand students’ freedom of expression and right to association, following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s call for the repeal of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU). MOHE said it had reviewed measures that could be implemented under the existing legal framework to give effect to the prime minister’s directive. It identified several provisions under AUKU and the Student Disciplinary Rules that restrict students’ freedom of expression and association for exemption from enforcement as immediate measures.

items.title: Ahmad Zahid extends condolences to families of Nepal flood victims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has expressed concern over the safety and well-being of Malaysians affected by the devastating floods in Nepal, hoping those still unaccounted for will be found safe and reunited with their families. Ahmad Zahid also extended his condolences to families who lost loved ones in the disaster, while expressing solidarity with the people of Nepal. “I am deeply saddened by the devastating flash floods in Nepal, which have claimed lives, displaced families and caused widespread destruction.

items.title: Kuching storm blows off roof at Sarawak deputy premier’s family home
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 28 — The roof of Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Dr Sim Kui Hian’s family house was blown off in a storm that hit several areas in Kuching yesterday. In a Facebook post, Dr Sim said he was in Bintulu when the incident occurred and was thankful that everyone at the house was safe. He said several houses in the surrounding areas, including a mall, were also affected by the storm.

items.title: Putrajaya, six states across Malaysia at risk of worsening haze through Aug 31, MetMalaysia says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Several areas across Malaysia remain at risk of hazy conditions and reduced visibility from August 27 to 31, according to weather forecast models monitored by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia). “The MyCMAQ (Malaysia Community Multi-scale Air Quality Model) haze concentration forecast shows Sarawak could be the worst-affected area, with most districts expected to experience hazy weather at the Unhealthy level. He said hazy conditions were expected in Sabah from Saturday, while high haze concentrations could affect Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya until August 31.

items.title: Two killed in Proton X70 crash while fleeing police checkpoint in Gua Musang
items.summary: Gua Musang district police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo said police received a report about the crash at 10.24 am. He said initial investigations found that police officers were conducting snap checks at Kilometre 16 of Jalan Gua Musang-Kuala Lipis when they spotted a suspicious-looking Proton X70, which then turned back towards Gua Musang town. Sik said one man died at the scene, while another died while receiving treatment at Gua Musang Hospital.

items.title: Viral video of cockroaches in food container prompts DBKL to shut BBQ outlet for 14 days (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — A video showing several insects believed to be cockroaches crawling inside a food container at a barbecue restaurant in the capital went viral on social media yesterday. Before eating, check your food first,” she wrote. Following the video’s circulation and attention on social media, Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) conducted an inspection of the premises.

items.title: Haze worsens as 18 areas across Malaysia, including KL, Putrajaya, record unhealthy air quality
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Air quality worsened across the country this morning, with 18 areas recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 7am. Sarikei and Miri also recorded unhealthy readings of 152 and 102 respectively. In the Klang Valley, Cheras and Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded API readings of 159 and 153 respectively, while Putrajaya recorded a reading of 152.

items.title: Nepal police release names of 23 Malaysians missing in deadly flood disaster
items.summary: HYDERABAD, Aug 28 — The Nepal Police on Thursday released the names of those missing in the flood catastrophe, including foreign nationals. A partial list of the missing available on the Nepal Police’s Facebook page as of 1 pm local time has the names of eight females and 15 males from Malaysia. Mohd Fakhrul Munir Bin Mohd Isa, 44 2.

items.title: Temenggor, Gerik hit by 3.4-magnitude earthquake
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — A weak 3.4-magnitude earthquake struck the Temenggor area in Gerik, Perak at 12.06am today, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia). MetMalaysia said the earthquake occurred at a depth of 10km at coordinates 5.5 degrees North and 101.3 degrees East, reported Astro Awani. Tremors were reportedly felt in several areas around Gerik.
